chapter: The Second Herd and its sidemen
title: Experimenting on the bandstand, not by plan
summary: Herman says his innovations are never planned but mostly done on the bandstand.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Tell me, even though you began with the original motivation and interest, because you heard Ernie Royal, how did you conceptualize this direction of being innovative in some sense here, and incorporating many of the things that were in the forefront of the music? Was that part of when you were reorganizing it? Did you rethink about --
These things are not planned, not in my case, at least. No, no, I can't have a big psyching out session and then go ahead and do it.
Now, a lot of my experimentation, 99 percent of the time has been done on the bandstand, and it's a very natural kind of thing.
